A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the TAS and OSTBC schemes, a sum rate comparable with the full feedback scheme can be obtained with an FB RB of 2, while for CDD, an FB RB of only 1.5 is sufficient.
for a given NFB, TAS outperforms OSTBC and CDD in terms of FB RB and for a given FB RB, TAS outperfo rms OSTBC and C DD in terms of NFB.

for the TAS and CDD schemes, the feedback ratio is independent of the number of users and is only a function of NFB and the number of transmit antennas, while for the OSTBC scheme it is also dependent on the number of users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
joint scheduling and diversity is able to achieve sum rates close to those achieved by a full feedback system, while only requiring a fraction of the feedback.
for a reduced feedback scheme, the feedback ratio can be as low as 1.5% and still achieve a sum rate close to the sum rate for the full feedback scheme.
joint scheduling and diversity is able to provide the same sum rate as a system with full feedback for a significantly lower feedback ratio.
